items.claim: One team modeled usable seismic data from 12 of 96 observatories.
items.synthesisExcerpt: One team studied seismic recordings from 96 observatories and digitized and modeled usable data from 12.
items.sourceEvidence: Operator paraphrase: “One team studied seismic recordings from 96 observatories and digitized and modeled usable data from 12.”
items.usefulness: Shows the data scope behind the seismic estimate.
items.qualification: The synthesis does not explain why data from only 12 observatories were usable.

items.claim: The seismic analysis suggested a surface-wave magnitude of 7.7.
items.synthesisExcerpt: That seismic analysis suggested a surface-wave magnitude of 7.7.
items.sourceEvidence: Operator paraphrase: “That seismic analysis suggested a surface-wave magnitude of 7.7.”
items.usefulness: Provides one side of the magnitude-estimate contrast.
items.qualification: Identified specifically as a surface-wave magnitude.

items.claim: A USGS team re-evaluated geodetic measurements from before and after the earthquake.
items.synthesisExcerpt: A USGS team instead re-evaluated geodetic measurements made before and after the earthquake.
items.sourceEvidence: Operator paraphrase: “A USGS team instead re-evaluated geodetic measurements made before and after the earthquake.”
items.usefulness: Introduces the contrasting approach used for the other estimate.
items.qualification: The synthesis does not provide further details about the re-evaluation.

items.claim: The geodetic approach used ground deformation measured through benchmark angles and distances and gave an estimate of 7.9.
items.synthesisExcerpt: The geodetic approach used ground deformation reflected in angles and distances between benchmarks and gave an estimate of 7.9.
items.sourceEvidence: Operator paraphrase: “The geodetic approach used ground deformation reflected in angles and distances between benchmarks and gave an estimate of 7.9.”
items.usefulness: Provides the other estimate and the measurement basis.
items.qualification: The synthesis does not specify the magnitude scale for 7.9.

items.claim: Different methods of estimating earthquake size can produce different estimates.
items.synthesisExcerpt: Different methods of estimating earthquake size can disagree.
items.sourceEvidence: Operator paraphrase: “Different methods of estimating earthquake size can disagree.”
items.usefulness: States the central takeaway supported by the contrasting estimates.
items.qualification: The synthesis does not explain the specific cause of the difference.

uncertainties: The supplied source evidence is labeled an operator paraphrase, not the source text itself.
The synthesis does not explain why the estimates differ or identify the magnitude scale for the 7.9 estimate.

operatorSourceAudit.locator: M = 7.7, M = 7.9, and Why can't scientists agree
operatorSourceAudit.evidence: Seismic waves were recorded at 96 observatories, and 12 stations had records suitable for digitization and modeling. Those results suggested surface-wave magnitude 7.7. USGS re-evaluated geodetic measurements from before and after the event, assessing deformation with benchmark distances and angles. Their slip models suggested moment magnitude 7.9. The methods estimate earthquake size differently.
